title: 十二时辰水法 Shi'er shichen shuifa
subtitle: Xiyang Lou

model.line: Simple massing of a European palace, assumed: sizes from the texts and the ruin polygons, position from the plan or the ruin. Not a reading of the 1786 engravings yet.

evidence.title: Plate X: 海晏堂 Haiyan Tang, west, and the water clock
evidence.excerpt_other: Sur deux des côtés du triangle, sont placés douze animaux de différentes espèces, six de chaque côté.
evidence.summary: Ten bays with a central block and attic and end pavilions; a landing with two stairs, jets from vases along both ramps as at St Cloud and Versailles. A triangular basin; animals spout towards the centre; at the apex towards the building a rock group with a shell; the largest jet from a vase at the base; two pyramids at the sides. He says animals spout by hour count.

evidence.title: Engraving 10: 海晏堂 Haiyan Tang, west front and water clock
evidence.excerpt_other: There two broad staircases one swinging to the right and one to the left, met before the main entrance on the level of the second floor.
evidence.summary: Largest of the group; held Benoist's pumps and the main reservoir. Fifty small jets on the stair balustrades fed three basins. Twelve seated animal figures, one for each two-hour period, spouted in turn to a larger fountain in the pool. After Benoist's death the machinery failed and water was raised by buckets and ropes (Benoist 1786, Amiot 1787, per n.). Malone compares bronze figures in the Winter Palace, made later.
